summary.headline: Kuantum Q1 FY27 operational income rose 36% YoY to INR304 crore, but EBITDA was flat at INR40 crore (13.2% margin) as input costs outran price gains.
summary.overview: Paper sales volume grew 35% YoY to 42,922 metric tons, and blended NSR improved about INR3,400/ton QoQ. Cost per ton rose about INR4,200 QoQ on raw material, chemical and fuel inflation linked to the West Asia conflict, so EBITDA stayed broadly flat YoY and PAT was INR6 crore. Management cut its FY27 top-line expectation to INR1,300 crore-plus from the earlier INR1,400-1,500 crore and pushed the 16-18% EBITDA margin target to the year-end. PM3 rebuild completion, pulp capacity additions and anti-dumping applications were the main operational updates.

segments.name: Paper (writing & printing, copier, maplitho)
segments.commentary: Realisation around INR68,000-69,000/ton per management, targeted to reach INR72,000-75,000 in 4-6 months. Specialty grades are just under 20% of mix (18-19% stated), target 30%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top line revised to INR1,300 crore-plus, versus earlier INR1,400-1,500 crore guidance; management said realisations are running below earlier expected levels.
EBITDA margin at least 16-18% by year-end; management says Q3 onwards is when these margins should be visible, not Q2.
FY28 top line expected INR1,400-1,500 crore; FY29-30 conservatively INR1,500 crore at current pricing, INR1,600-1,650 crore if pricing rises to about INR75,000/ton.
Peak debt about INR760-770 crore; scheduled repayments about INR170-175 crore per year for the next 2-3 years; debt to fall below INR300-350 crore within 3 years.
AI-led opex reduction target of 4-5% by March 2028.
Pulp capacity to rise to about 410-415 TPD from 365 TPD.
capex_capacity: DDS (Double Displacement Digester) for wood pulping commissioned in Q1.
Native starch system commissioned on PM2 and PM3.
Folio ream wrapping machine installed in the finishing house.
PM3 shut for major rebuild; management expects commissioning within about a week of the call (mid-August 2026), completing the upgradation programme.
Pulping capacity of about 200 TPD each for agro and wood, said to be sufficient for all four machines.
EC clearance for PM3 upgrade filed and awaited.
Clonal propagation: record 17.28 lakh saplings in the quarter; plantation area about 19,650 acres after adding about 1,300 acres.
demand_pricing: Demand supported by education, publishing and office consumption; management expects demand to stay supportive.
Chinese imports diminishing, attributed mainly to shipping and container cost issues; imported copier/maplitho price seen at $610-620/ton near port.
Anti-dumping and anti-subsidy duty applications filed for writing and printing paper, covering 40-140 GSM; management hopes for a favourable decision, assumed 5-year duration.
Maplitho hit by inverted duty structure after GST change; management says Kuantum is reducing notebook paper exposure and passing GST losses to customers.
Management says pricing held flat QoQ into Q2 with no discounting; dealer channel inventory described as lean.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance maintained, and what EBITDA margin is achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is positive with PM3 commissioning, targeting at least 16-18% EBITDA margin by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is peak debt and the repayment path?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak debt about INR760-770 crore; repayments of about INR170-175 crore a year for 2-3 years, with debt below INR300 crore within 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the revenue guidance fall from INR1,400-1,500 crore to INR1,300 crore-plus?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisations are running below earlier expected levels and EBITDA margins are strained by West Asia-driven costs; management says figures are conservative.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall while a competitor's rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to Punjab-specific raw material cost increases, mainly wheat straw, which it says is easing; it expects a gradual reduction in procurement cost.

qa_highlights.question: What share of cost increase is due to the West Asia crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% of the INR4,200/ton cost increase is attributed to West Asia; INR3,400/ton has been passed through in pricing QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Will wheat straw prices come down?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said procurement prices fell in Q2 versus Q1 after negotiations with suppliers, with further easing expected as rice straw and corn cobs arrive in September-October.

risks_watch: Cost pass-through: about INR800/ton of the INR4,200/ton cost rise was not recovered in Q1 price gains; watch whether Q2 NSR and margins recover.
Execution on PM3 commissioning (mid-August) and full-capacity ramp; Q2 is expected to be weak with machine and boiler shutdowns.
Revenue guidance cut and inconsistency with earlier FY28-30 projections.
Q2 seasonally weak demand; management says October onwards is when the industry picks up.
Pending EC clearance for PM3 and pending anti-dumping and anti-subsidy duty decision.
Debt of about INR760-770 crore at peak and interest burden on PAT.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term capacity and specialty mix, but defensive on the FY27 numbers: management conceded the revenue guidance was revised and that margins are being squeezed by costs outside its control. Answers on the guidance gap and FY30 targets were partly contradictory and hard to reconcile.
key_quotes: We should be reaching closer to about at least between 16% to 18% by the year-end.
Peak debt, we are currently looking at about INR760 crores or INR770 crores maximum.
Nobody could have imagined like a war starting in a part of the world and impacting sort of pricing here in India.
Right now, our contribution from specialty paper is just under 20%.

growth.why: FY27 top line cut to INR1,300 crore-plus from the earlier INR1,400-1,500 crore guidance, roughly 8% below the earlier low end of about INR1,400 crore, with Q1 volumes up 35% YoY but realisations running below plan; PM3 restart and pulp expansion support volume growth, offset by pricing and margin pressure.
